summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour addresses the Muslim Community Center of Tucson, reflecting on six months of studying Islamic purification (tahara) directly from Quranic and Sunnah sources. He emphasizes the importance of learning from primary sources rather than relying on incidental knowledge passed down through generations, comparing this to the children's game of telephone where messages become distorted. Sh. Ali Mashhour explains that the community has completed studying wudu and ghusl (the two forms of purification with water) and will now move to tayammum (purification with soil). He addresses the common excuse of being too busy by highlighting that the Companions were far more occupied with daily survival tasks yet still made time for learning, and he discusses how Allah sends revivalist scholars every 100 years to preserve and clarify Islamic knowledge. Sh. Ali Mashhour concludes by outlining the curriculum ahead: tayammum, salah, zakat, fasting, and eventually hajj and umrah.
